title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the verso (T.S.V.P.) of Grothendieck's p. 595, inside his 'équation des lacets' material. That material is his own version of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group Γ_Q^~ (written M, M[σ]) acting on the profinite fundamental group Π_0^∧ of a configuration such as P^1−{0,1,∞}. Its elements u are normalised by 'base-point' relations (BP) on two inertia generators ρ and σ:
- u(ρ) is conjugate to ρ^{ε3} by α;
- u(σ) = ε2 int(β) σ, i.e. u(σ) = int(β)(σ^{ε2}) with β ∈ Π_0^∧ unique (after normalisation).
On p. 595 he wrote these as a = α^{-1}u ∈ Z_ρ^♮ and b = β^{-1}u ∈ N'_σ, computed inside the semidirect product Π^∧ ⋊ Aut. He suspected, from the developments of §48, that a, b and the sign data might depend multiplicatively on u, and announced that this fails.

This page checks the multiplicative part.
(1) For u, u' one gets (u'u)(σ) = u'(int(β)σ^{ε2}) = int(u'(β)) u'(σ)^{ε2} = int(u'(β)β') σ^{ε2ε2'}. By uniqueness of β this gives (45): β'' = u'(β)β' and ε2'' = ε2'ε2. So u ↦ β is a crossed homomorphism (1-cocycle) of the automorphism group with values in Π_0^∧.
(2) Equivalently b'' = b'b. In the semidirect product, u'β^{-1} = u'(β^{-1})u', so β''^{-1}u'u = β'^{-1}u'β^{-1}u is equivalent to β''^{-1} = β'^{-1}u'(β^{-1}), i.e. to (45). Hence u ↦ b is a genuine homomorphism.
(3) ε3'' = ε3'ε3 is clear from (46): u(ρ) is conjugate to ρ^{ε3}.
(4) The remaining question is the hypothetical relation a'' = a'a. It would imply (A): δ(a'') = δ(a')δ(a), where δ: G_{ρ,σ} ≅ M → Γ_Q-like quotient. But (43), (43 bis) and (43 ter) give δ(u) = τ_γ^{ν3}δ(a), δ(u') = τ_γ^{ν3'}δ(a') and δ(u'u) = τ_γ^{ν3''}δ(a''). Multiplying gives δ(u')δ(u) = τ^{ν3'}δ(a')τ^{ν3}δ(a).

On the next page he concludes:
- δ(a'') = τ^{ν3}(δ(a'))·δ(a), with τ^{ν3} acting by conjugation;
- so a'' = a'a holds iff δ(u') commutes with τ_γ^{ν3}.
When ε3 = −1 this means δ(u') centralises the 'complex conjugation' τ_γ. He calls this a draconian condition, which he expects forces δ(u') ∈ {1, τ_γ}. Hence u ↦ a is a homomorphism essentially only in the abelian (cyclotomic Ẑ^*) situation, where τ_γ is central.
errors: Last displayed line reads δ(u'u'') = τ^{ν3''}δ(a''); it should be δ(u'u) = δ(u''). This is a slip.

On p. 595, (43) has exponent τ_γ^{ε3} while (43 bis)/(43 ter) use τ_γ^{ν3}. If τ_γ is an involution, only the ν3 ∈ Z/2 exponent makes sense, so this is a notational inconsistency, not a mathematical error.
In (4) one tacitly uses ν3'' = ν3' + ν3, established via (46); that step is fine.

ideas.what: u ↦ β (the conjugator normalising u(σ)) satisfies β'' = u'(β)β', i.e. a crossed homomorphism; equivalently u ↦ b = β^{-1}u is a homomorphism into the semidirect product.
ideas.modern_name: 1-cocycle / crossed homomorphism; composition law in GT^ written as (λ,f)·(λ',f')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for the GT composition law; Ihara for the Galois-side cocycle viewpoint

ideas.what: Signs ε2, ε3 (orientation characters at the two punctures) are multiplicative.
ideas.modern_name: sign/orientation character of the extended (Z/2-enlarged) GT group

ideas.what: The 'inertia-side' normaliser a = α^{-1}u is NOT multiplicative. The defect is the conjugation action of τ_γ (complex conjugation) on δ(u'), so multiplicativity holds iff δ(u') centralises τ_γ.
ideas.modern_name: non-split cocycle twisted by complex conjugation; centraliser of complex conjugation in GT^ / extended GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (centraliser of complex conjugation in G_Q = {1,c} is classical, Artin–Schreier type)

missed.claim: This page and the next lead to a heuristic expectation: in Grothendieck's GT-like group Γ_Q^~, the centraliser of the complex-conjugation element τ_γ is {1, τ_γ}, as in G_Q. If so, a naive multiplicative presentation (that of §48) works only in the abelian cyclotomic case. A self-centralising complex conjugation in (extended) GT^ is a natural question; I am not sure it is settled in the literature.
missed.quote: Il reste donc à examiner la relation hypothétique a'' = a'a qui implique δ(a'') = δ(a')δ(a)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This concerns the open comparison of G_Q with GT^. Whether order-2 elements of GT^ are self-centralising (as in absolute Galois groups) is a testable group-theoretic analogue.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine cocycle verification and sets up a non-multiplicativity check. The only potentially interesting point is the conjecture it leads to (on the next page) about the centraliser of complex conjugation in a GT-like group, which is stated heuristically.
transcription_corrections: This sheet is the verso of Grothendieck's p. 595 (it ends 'T.S.V.P.' and the next page is 596); '583' is the archive number.
Opening line likely 'On sait que' / 'On a vu que' rather than 'On [?] a [?]'.
'ce qui par l'unicité prouve' is fine; read 'd'où on conclut bien'.
In (46) the illegible prefix before '-conj.' is unclear in the image; it is likely a group symbol (e.g. Π^∧- or 𝒞^{+1}-), not 'C^{v+1}'. A word under 'de ρ^{ε3}' is struck out.
Last line should read δ(u'u) = δ(u'') = τ_γ^{ν3''}δ(a'') (the manuscript has the slip δ(u'u'')).
The relation involving δ(u')δ(u) begins with a struck-out mark.
